look_here_first: Start at a middle or upper leaf node: the opposite narrow leaves have rounded ear-like (auriculate), often clasping bases. Follow the leaf axil to a loose, stalked cyme with several tiny flowers; inspect the ribbed floral tube, then a mature globose capsule. Compare cluster stalk length and leaf bases with A. coccinea.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Kew treats A. auriculata as accepted and native in Texas; three target-zone counties not independently established.

morphology_keys.habit: Erect, branched annual wetland herb, usually about 15–65 cm tall; upper stems four-angled.
morphology_keys.leaves: Opposite, sessile, narrow-lanceolate to oblong-lanceolate, often 1.5–8 cm long; bases typically heart-shaped with ear-like lobes that clasp the stem.
morphology_keys.flowers: Small pink-purple flowers in loose, stalked axillary cymes, often 3–15 flowers; four sepals; floral tube about 1–2 mm long, 4–8-ribbed; petals may be short-lived.
morphology_keys.fruit: Nearly spherical capsule, roughly 1.5–3.5 mm across, with numerous small seeds; confirm against persistent calyx.

comparisons.key_distinctions: A. auriculata commonly has longer slender peduncles carrying loose multi-flowered axillary cymes; A. coccinea tends to have more compact flower groups. Check mature calyx/capsule and leaf-base shape together, not flower color alone. Rotala has a different leaf-base/floral configuration; verify with reproductive parts.
